properties.statement:
BINDING-VERSUS-VISIBLE IS ALREADY DECIDED BY A FIELD THAT EXISTS. Measured 2026-08-29 by running the REAL `check_intent_authority.py` against three hand-built export documents, each simulating a hub Decision arriving in a child design by mirroring.

    CASE                                                    GATE      what it means
    A  accepted, approver edge dropped                      FAIL (1)  what mirroring produces TODAY
    B  accepted + hub owner's Contributor + approver edge    OK   (0)  BINDING — named authority
    C  arrives as `proposed`, reasoning intact               OK   (0)  VISIBLE — asserts nothing locally

🛑 ① "VISIBLE IS THE CHEAP OPTION" WAS FALSE AS I HAD FRAMED IT, and this refutes my own recommendation from earlier the same day. I argued visible-only needs none of the machinery binding needs. But `settles_intent()` reads ONLY `status == "accepted"` — it never looks at `GOVERNED_BY`. So a mirrored accepted Decision trips the enforced rule whether or not it governs anything in the child. There is no free version of "just let them see it" if what arrives is still marked accepted.

⭐ ② AND THE SWITCH IS THE STATUS FIELD, NOT A NEW MECHANISM. Case C needs nothing built beyond making Decision publishable: a hub decision arriving as `proposed` is READABLE — name, statement, rationale, alternatives all intact — and asserts nothing in the child's graph. That is not a workaround; it is literally true. The hub's settled intent is the child's OPEN QUESTION, and the child owner accepting it is the local ruling. Case B is then the binding form, and it costs exactly one thing: the approver Contributor must travel in the published surface so the edge survives. No gate change, no `provenance: imported` awareness — B passed with the stock gate untouched.

③ THE GATE ITSELF NAMED CASE C AND I HAD NOT CONSIDERED IT. Its failure message offers three honest remedies: get the approver, move the status back to `proposed`, or (refused) add the id to the grandfathered set. The second is the whole visible design, written in an error string, and I read past it twice.

🛑 BOUNDS, and the first one narrows an overstatement I made this morning. `check_intent_authority.py` is REFLOW2-ONLY — it is not installed into consumer projects, which get `reflow2_check.py`. So "the child's build fails" is true of reflow2 self-hosting and NOT automatically true of a user's child design; whether their graph enforces the same rule is theirs to say. What survives unbounded is the doctrine rather than the tooling: an accepted Decision with nobody's name on it is a forged signature, and that is `dec:certainty-derived`, not a python script.

ALSO NOT ESTABLISHED: whether a reader on the far side actually GETS VALUE from an inherited rationale. That was the experiment originally proposed and this is not it — this measures what the machinery permits, not what a person finds useful. It is the cheaper question and it had to be answered first, because two of the three crossings were not available at all.
